gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: If the alarm sounds, ___ the building immediately.
gaps.hint: an instruction after if, imperative result
gaps.explanation: Instructions after 'if' keep the present simple in the if-clause and use the imperative as the result: leave.

gaps.sentence: If I had known you were coming, I ___ a cake.
gaps.hint: unreal past result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition is 'would have' plus the past participle: would have baked.

gaps.sentence: If dogs ___ wings, they would fly.
gaps.hint: an impossible present, past simple if-clause
gaps.explanation: Impossible present conditions still take the past simple after 'if': had.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: Unless it ___ below five degrees tonight, the event will go ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple even when referring to tonight: drops.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.
